records.title: Request Message (Commands)
records.source_span_text:
5.0 Request Message (Commands)
 The Request message is used to send commands from one component to another. The
 structure used for this is the Request composite type. When issuing a command using the
 Request type, it is necessary to include the name of the command along with parameters.

 In the ISA Data Model, a there is a single Request type that is used for all commands. The
 command field in the type is used for providing the command name. The parameters field is
 a list of the NVP composite type. Each NVP in the parameter list holds the name (NVP
 name) and value (NVP value) of a single parameter.

 IPL Format 3 treats Standard Commands and Custom Commands differently. For Standard
 Commands, each of the commands is represented by a different composite type. The
 composite type is given the name of the command, and the fields within the type are the
 parameters to the command. To deal with custom commands, the Custom Request
 composite type is used. The Command field in the custom type is used for providing the
 command name. The parameters field is a list of the NVP composite type. Each NVP in the
 parameter list holds the name (NVP name) and value (NVP value) of a single parameter. All

 request structures are part of the Request union type.




                                                                                              6

native_rules.rule: Request sends commands from one component to another and includes command identity and parameters.
A single Data Model Request type uses command for the command name and parameters as a list of NVPs, one parameter name/value in each NVP.
Each standard command has a separate composite named for the command, whose fields are its parameters.
Custom commands use Custom Request with Command for the name and a parameters NVP list.
All request structures are members of the Request union.

limitations: The Data Model Request composite, the Format 3 Request union and the higher-level DMS Message union must not be collapsed into one schema.
The guide supplies no union discriminator tag values, byte layout, generated schema, per-command parameter table or full Request-common-field mapping.
The generic command name plus parameters discussion does not require a nonempty parameter list; completed DMS Request evidence permits 0+ parameters.
Encoding a request is neither declaring support for a command nor proof of permission, execution, success or physical effect.

records.title: Lists
records.source_span_text:
6.0 Lists
 In IPL Format 3, there is an ambiguity when dealing with lists. The absence of a list (no list)
 and the empty list (zero length) are encoded in the same way. The receiver will not know if
 the list is not being provided because there is no update, or if the list is being updated to an
 empty list.

 To resolve this, additional fields are added to the Status and Event structures. For each list-
 based property and observable, an associated Boolean exists to indicate if the list is being
 supplied. The name of the field ends in _supplied. For example, the Wavelengths property
 has an associated wavelengths_property_supplied field. When true, that property indicates
 the information in the Wavelengths field is the value for that property, even if empty.




                                                                                                7
records.source_locator: ISA IPL3 Usage Guide 6.0r4 / 31 October 2023, §6.0 Lists; PDF pages 13; printed pages 7

native_rules.rule: The absence of a list and an empty list have the same encoding; a receiver cannot otherwise know whether no update was provided or the value was updated to an empty list.
Additional fields are added to Status and Event: each list-based property or observable has an associated Boolean indicating whether the list is supplied.
The associated Boolean field name ends in _supplied.
When wavelengths_property_supplied is true, information in the Wavelengths field is the property value even if empty.

limitations: The guide explicitly supplies the true case; it does not specify a default, serialization behavior for an omitted flag, or a full false/absent truth table.
The Boolean is a provided-value indication, not authorization, quality, support, readiness, data validity or successful execution.
Do not generalize the workaround to every list anywhere in the Data Model; the described additions are list-based properties/observables in Status/Event.
The example does not provide actual wavelength numbers, a per-command list rule or a physical sensor claim.
Existing DMS List remains an empty-capable value collection; encoding presence is a distinct information pattern, not a change to its values cardinality.

front_matter_review.source_text:
Executive Summary

The Integrated Sensor Architecture (ISA) is developed by the Army Program Executive
Officer for Intelligence, Electronic Warfare and Sensors (PEO IEW&S). The primary goal of
ISA is to enable systems to readily integrate into an existing network and dynamically share
data, information, and capabilities to help achieve situational awareness.

ISA is designed to make systems and their capabilities dynamically discoverable and
available to soldiers and platforms, without prior knowledge or specific integration, and
regardless of system type or ownership. This design maximizes access to useful data and
functionality, while minimizing integration complexity and lifecycle costs.

ISA is an interoperability solution designed to accomplish data, information, and capability
sharing within a tactical environment. ISA applies standards and technologies to address the
highly constrained communications, ever-changing conditions, and cybersecurity demands
that are characteristic of the tactical domain.

With the advent of the Army Common Operating Environment (COE) to eliminate the
capability shortfalls, cost overruns, and schedule delays that are common for system
acquisition, the Sensor Computing Environment (CE) was created to achieve sensor
interoperability across the Army’s tactical and enterprise realms. Specifically, Sensor CE is
defined to enable dynamic discovery of sensors, distribution of observation-related alerts,
dissemination of motion imagery, and control of sensors. Given ISA’s abilities and qualities,
ISA was chosen as the main material solution for Sensor CE.

master_revisions.reason: ISA component is defined by interface and behavioral conformance. A Controller is a component providing core services. Connection roles are contextual; an ISA component is not necessarily one physical device or one operating-system process.

ISA composition member = integration membership; physical part-of not established

master_revisions.reason: A composition member is any component in the integration collection except the CIC. It may be ISA-compliant or use a native interface. The source does not establish a physical part-of relationship.

display: ISA component: virtual node; Client / Controller roles; Controller software responsibilities
before.definition: A network participant has client or Controller responsibilities, separately from the generic identity of the participant and any physical equipment it represents.
before.boundary: A Controller is software; a component may be a sensor, adapter, base station or command-and-control system. A virtual node is not necessarily one physical device. The original network-participant mapping receives supporting evidence but retains its broader architecture reconciliation assignment.

display: All ISA components support the client-side connection role; Controllers also support the server-side role
after.definition: Client-side and server-side identify roles in a connection. Every ISA component, including a Controller, supports initiating connections to a Controller; Controllers also accept connections.
after.boundary: The initiator is the client and the non-initiator is the server for that connection. Controller is a service responsibility and software role; it also has client-side responsibilities. These are not disjoint equipment classes, physical device counts or process counts. A visible network participant need not equal one physical device.

master_revisions.reason: Detailed SDD roles refine the introductory Client/Controller shorthand without changing source meaning or making a case implementation claim.

before.definition: A participant belongs to a virtual network instance and communicates through the described connections; instances may interconnect across locations.
before.boundary: The guide diagrams describe connectivity and virtual participation, not physical containment, a deployment inventory or a tested topology. High-level examples do not settle detailed composition, routing or deployment rules assigned to the Software Design Document review.

after.definition: A local ISA instance and the broader network describe virtual participation and connections; local Controller/client instances may interconnect across locations.
after.boundary: The Introductory Guide local instance has one Controller and clients. SDD describes a broader network of interconnected components and Controllers over existing physical networks, with one or many Controllers in a deployment. Do not make a local instance a global one-Controller limit or infer physical containment, an actual deployment inventory, tested topology or mandatory full-mesh connectivity.

master_revisions.reason: Reconcile local-instance guidance with the broader distributed network architecture; the existing local-instance cell remains correctly scoped.

before.boundary: Six DMS service definitions are not six mandatory Controller modules. White Paper 4.3 identifies Communication, Live Data and Authorization as core Controller services and Historical Data as an additional configured service. Empty property/observable columns do not prohibit additional capabilities. Support, provider selection, requests and actual execution remain distinct.

after.boundary: Six DMS service definitions are not six mandatory Controller modules. SDD 4.2.1 requires each ISA 6.0 Controller to support all three core services, while support and activation are distinct; 5.0 separately describes typical hosting. Any component may provide optional services. Empty property/observable columns do not prohibit additional capabilities. Support, activation, provider selection, authorization, request, execution and achieved effects remain separate.

master_revisions.reason: Preserve must-support, may-activate, typical-hosting and optional-service distinctions without changing any DMS command list.

initial_catalogue_review_context.scope: Exactly6 DMS services and24 capability-bin entries001–030; companion guides integrated separately.

display: Request.request id ≠ separate identifier; Response.reference → Request identifier
Command request identity and response reference
before.boundary: Response.reference prose does not explicitly select request id over identifier; no equality or conversion is invented.

display: Request.request id and identifier remain separate; ICD6.7.1 sets Response.reference to Request ID; DMS wording retained
Command request identity and response reference
after.boundary: ICD6.7.1 explicitly requires Response.reference to equal the command Request ID and the Envelope To field to address the caller. The preserved DMS309 text says Identifier of the Request message without naming request id; retain that source-specific wording and the separate Request.identifier field. No invented identifier equality,conversion or executed exchange is claimed.

master_revisions.reason: Add the explicit interface correlation rule without silently rewriting the less-specific DMS definition or deleting its historical wording note.

display: Negotiated presentation = message-encoding technology + ISA data-model schema version; IPL negotiates and carries messages
Negotiated message encoding and model version
before.definition: After establishing a secure connection, a component and Controller negotiate the message encoding and the version of the data model used for their exchanges.
before.boundary: SDD §6.2 (6.0r5) lists Protocol Buffers/XML and IPv4/IPv6, TCP and TLS. These are edition-specific architectural statements, not selected deployed settings, tested security, wire-format details or physical interfaces. ICD/IPL/certificate details retain their next-delivery assignment.

display: IPL protocol v1; negotiated presentation/schema byte pair; long/short forms and separate Custom Java API format
Negotiated message encoding and model version
after.definition: The connection negotiates a supported presentation/schema byte pair,while the IPL protocol version remains a separate value; schema form and encoded representation do not replace the underlying information meaning.
after.boundary: ICD6.0r5 supports IPL protocol version1 and lists Protocol Buffers/XML long and short forms plus0x05/0x01 Custom Java API encoding. Unsupported/deprecated format pairs and inconsistent printed examples retain their source standing. IPL3 transforms standard capabilities into dedicated declarations/fields/request types while custom content retains generic structures. Neither IPL Format3 nor its schema byte is protocol version3. No actual negotiation,schema-file validation or current security result is asserted.

master_revisions.reason: Refine the completed SDD presentation pattern with the assigned interface formats and IPL3 transformations; preserve wire/payload/version distinctions.

before.boundary: Report content is distinct from Get Config request, property measurements and actual command effects.

after.boundary: Declarations and readiness/reporting states remain distinct from current Status values and performed work. ICD7.3 says a modifiable property is marked mutable in the CCD; clearing it makes it Not Ready,and not-ready properties must be Not Reporting and absent from Status. The DMS Clear Property precondition remains a value previously supplied through Set Property; its null-value consequence is retained. This does not establish deletion of historical data or physical absence. IPL3 declaration representations do not change the saved DMS declaration contracts.

master_revisions.reason: Record the explicit mutability/readiness/reporting relationship while retaining the full DMS Config schema.

before.boundary: Distinct from a Get Status request, Config state records and Event observables.

after.boundary: Distinct from a Get Status request, Config states and Event observables. ICD 6.5 gives general Status publication bounds through Minimum/Maximum Status Interval and contextual significant change. The saved DMS Threshold Declaration also specifies threshold publication regardless of status interval; retain both source statements without inventing precedence. IPL3 encodes standard properties as optional typed fields and custom properties through the named-value structure; list presence is separate from list contents. The DMS Status.properties list remains unchanged.

master_revisions.reason: Reconcile information meaning with encoding-specific representation and current availability,without replacing the DMS message schema.

before.boundary: No standalone type field is invented in Name Value Pair; a named value is not automatically a physical transducer or a performed observation.

after.boundary: No standalone type field is invented in Name Value Pair. The generic DMS uses named values in Status,Event and Request payloads; IPL3 gives standard properties/observables typed fields and standard commands dedicated request structures,while custom content retains generic named structures. Semantic name/value meaning need not use the same encoded field shape. A named value is not a physical transducer or proof of a performed observation.

master_revisions.reason: Distinguish generic information-model payloads from the reviewed short-form encoding without inventing schema aliases or wire fields.

before.boundary: No automatic registration success, mandated credential scheme or security guarantee.

after.boundary: Registration.credentials is application-message data; it is distinct from the TLS certificate required by the ICD connection rules and the Certificate Guide trust/usage context. The saved DMS fields specify no automatic registration success or particular credential scheme. Possessing a certificate does not by itself establish a permitted command,successful registration or verified deployment security.

master_revisions.reason: Prevent transport-certificate requirements from being silently inserted into,or excluded by,the separate Registration.credentials message field.
